chapter.question: What will the people across the river make of a Vaelmark captain who comes running to their door, and what must he lay down to be let in?

slots.plan: The far bank, the first morning. Deep snow, old forest, no bells anywhere: Wren notices first. Behind them on the west bank the rider's horses stand and do not come onto the ice, and there is smoke over the reeds. The first clan thing on the page stands at the tree line: a lamp-post with its lamp cold, and a black chip on a thong tied round it, which Rae will not let Wren touch (plants: a lamp at every clan door; the burned chips, T4, first plant). Rae says her grandmother's word for this wood and stops there. She takes them in by her grandmother's way, the pass her grandmother came out by, with the cart on its frozen stream, because that is what a road is here in winter (her wrong call, set here: `rae.road`, b3.1).
slots.turn: Rae, nearer her grandmother's country than she has ever been, knows the first rule of it and has to decide to say so; Darrow, who led them over the ice, lets her lead off the bank.

slots.plan: The first full day in the forest. The trees close; the stream is the road. A watch that does not show itself walks beside them: ski-tracks that stop, a second lamp-post with its lamp burning in daylight, bread left on a stump that Rae says is not for them (*tal*, a gift before an ask, named; they have left none). Wren keeps a column for lamps since there are no bells to count. At dusk Hollis hears singing a long way off, a tune he half knows, and will not say from where. Darrow wants to call out; Rae says a guest does not shout at a door he has not found.
slots.turn: Darrow, who finds a line and breaks it, has to walk a whole day beside a watch he cannot see and leave the first word to someone else.

slots.plan: The watch shows itself at dusk, and not for them: lamps running along a ridge, a horn that is no bell, and one word shouted down through the trees that Rae goes white at and turns into their tongue: run. Something is in the trees behind, slow and many: her grandmother's pass has been the dark's own road for twenty years, and she knows it as she runs (her wrong call lands). The lamp line is a mile off down the stream ice. The first run that matters (a run on the flat ice, straight; no leap, no sprint, no turning at speed: Knot IV's allows). The company runs for the lamps; Darrow can, and finds inside a hundred strides that he is ahead of all of them, with the oxen and Hollis on the cart falling behind. Ends on the small choice.
slots.turn: The legs give him back the old speed in the one place it can cost him his own people; he must choose where to run.

micro.ask: He is ahead of all of them on the ice, with the lamps a mile off and the cart falling behind. What does Darrow do?
options: Drop back and run at the cart's tail, the last of them, beside Hollis.
Run on for the lamps and bring the watch back to them.
Stop on the ice with the lamp and the stick and let every one of them go past him first.

slots.plan: His answer played. The run ends inside the lamp line: the watch closes behind them with torches and long spears turned outward, not at them, and holds until the trees are quiet. Then the spears turn round. A dozen of the watch on skis, furred, laughing slowly at a Vaelmark captain out of breath with a walking stick; their leader asks one thing through Rae's few words: whose dog. Ash is looked at, fed and admired before anybody asks the company's names. Nobody says what was in the trees, and Rae does not ask: it is not named at night.
slots.turn: The company learns it ranks second to its own dog with the people who just saved it, and that those people have not decided to keep them; Darrow has to stand and be laughed at, and let it be funny.

slots.plan: A day under guard toward the holdfast, on ski-tracks through old forest, the cart on the stream. What the watch lets them see and does not explain: every one of them wears a black chip at the throat (the chips, second plant); a burned place in a clearing, wide as a threshing floor, that they pass with their eyes down. Rae says her grandmother's name aloud to the watch-leader, with the word for whose child's child she is; the leader stops walking. It buys a hearing and nothing yet beyond it (`rae.road`). Thread 5: the leader has heard of a Vaelmark knight pulled out of the ford alive, and looks at Darrow's face a moment too long.
slots.turn: Rae spends the one coin she has carried all her life, in front of him, without asking him first, because it is hers to spend; he has to be the one who is carried by it.

slots.plan: The holdfast: a wall of whole trunks, a lamp at every door and one at the gate bigger than the rest, dogs, children on the wall counting the strangers (Wren counts back). The hearing is at the gate, outside it. An elder asks through Rae what they bring, since a gift comes before an ask. The company has little: the last of the millers' flour, Maelis's salt, a ledger, a sword in oilcloth, a stick. Ends on the small choice: what Darrow gives.
slots.turn: He must make a gift to people who owe him nothing but a grave, and what he chooses to give tells them who has come.
slots.tone: wary, with a people who find him funny

micro.ask: A gift comes before an ask. What does Darrow give?
options: His name and what he is, said plainly as the first gift: the captain of the Ninth, from the ford, before they can find it out.
The company's stores, the flour and the salt, laid down by the carter's hand, and his own name left for another day.

slots.plan: The gift's answer, and the guest-fire outside the gate for the night: food carried out by children who want to touch the dog; the lamps lit along the wall at dusk one by one and counted aloud by the children, and by Wren; a ford-song sung on the wall that Hollis knows the other side of (grief, once, plain and short); Maelis asked to look at a clan child's hand and asked nothing else. Warm at a fire at last, with every eye on them. Late, word comes out from inside: tomorrow the gate opens to a guest, and a guest lays down his blade at the door.
slots.turn: Fed and warm for the first time since the river, Darrow learns the price of the roof a night before he is asked to pay it, and hears what each of his people would do.
slots.tone: warm, watched; grief once, plain and short

world_moves: The grey cloaks reach the marsh and camp on the causeway within sight of the ring; their censer smoke stands over the reeds all day, and nobody walks out on the ice to stop them looking.
The rider in the Second's colours turns her four horses south from the river bank, with a report nobody has asked her to shorten.
The millers come down to the villages below the mill with their flour and the story of the bridge, and the story walks faster than they do.

climax.plan: The holdfast door (b3.1's choice). By the tier: Triumph, the watch brings them to the door as guests of the bridge (word of the mill has crossed the river ahead of them); Hard-won, taken in under guard and fed anyway; Costly, two more days at the guest-fire before the door opens; Setback, taken in because Ash is hurt and it is the dog they want. The door-warden holds out her hands for the blade. The checks, then the choice; its Downstream sets how b3.2's telling is heard.
climax.tone: hospitable and watchful; a hall that fears the dark
checks: resolve (standing still at the gate while a people who sing about the ford look him over)
resolve (Warden's Eye: reading the door-warden, and what a laid-down blade means here)
vigor (the night outside the wall, and the cold)
options: Give up his sword at the door, laid down as a guest lays down a blade.
Keep it and stand outside the wall, owing them nothing.
Claim the hearth as kin: Rae's grandmother's name and household in his own mouth, said before Rae has decided to spend it.

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.

planted.text: Ser Oswin of the Fourth at Coldmere (ch05:s6): kneels at every stone the road gives him; lifted a cart off a boy with hands that frosted white and cleared without melting; offered Darrow the crossroads stone at first light with a full heart
